verdict.root_cause: At 03:37:46 UTC platform-automation rewrote cartservice's environment configuration so its Redis endpoint points at redis-cart port 6380 instead of the conventional 6379 (tr_9f124d3d02ef). cartservice resolves that endpoint during RedisCartStore.InitializeAsync at process start, cannot connect, and dies with an unhandled ApplicationException out of Main, restarting on a ~30-60s cycle from at least 03:42:57 through 03:45:04 (tr_37309257e4ed). With cartservice's listener absent for most of each cycle, checkoutservice's outbound CartService/GetCart call is refused immediately — every sampled checkout trace fails at that hop in 0.4-1.2ms with the error inherited upward to the frontend (tr_34e02e3f107e), and checkout's own logs show orders accepted after 03:40 but never reaching the payment, email or queue-write steps (tr_d0834463478d). The wrong port value is itself the failure: the request path breaks because the connection target names a port nothing is listening on. Downstream services named in triage (payment, currency, product catalog) are collateral non-participants — they are never reached in any failing trace (tr_34e02e3f107e) and show clean or zero error ratios (tr_1828e73c3100, tr_38879161549e, tr_a3e26d2df304).
verdict.reasoning: Three independent lines converge. Traces localize the originating error span to the checkoutservice-to-cartservice GetCart hop and rule out checkout's own logic, the frontend, and any timeout/latency mechanism — failures are sub-millisecond immediate refusals, not waits (tr_34e02e3f107e). Logs on cartservice name the failing dependency explicitly and place the failure in startup initialization, not request handling, with a repeating crash-restart cycle (tr_37309257e4ed). The change log supplies the only recorded mutation anywhere in the blast radius: an automation-issued env edit to the redis endpoint port, timestamped ~2.5 minutes before the alert (tr_9f124d3d02ef). Checkout's change log is empty (tr_6d2dbb9f0fa1), as are payment's and currency's (tr_38879161549e, tr_a3e26d2df304), so the trigger is not local to the alerting services. The absence of cartservice call metrics entirely — denominator included (tr_5cfa77c5594d, tr_be2f37cbfe4c) — is corroborating rather than contradictory: a process that dies during startup emits no spans, so flat-zero or empty cart error metrics must not be read as cart health, which is precisely the misread recorded in the cart-bad-image-tag corpus entry. I classify this bad_config rather than bad_deploy because no image or build changed (tr_9f124d3d02ef explicitly rules out a rollout) and the running artifact is the intended one; the wrongness of the port value is the mechanism. It is not dependency_latency because nothing is slow — the trace evidence rules out timeouts. It is not resource_exhaustion because nothing is being consumed to a limit. The fix is to revert the endpoint value, not to restart (restarts are already happening and do not help) and not to roll back an artifact.
open_questions: Nobody verified what redis-cart is actually listening on. If Redis legitimately moved to 6380 and cartservice's old value was stale, the correct fix is on the Redis side, not a revert of the cartservice env. tr_9f124d3d02ef records no prior value, so the pre-change state is unknown.

Why platform-automation issued this edit — what reconciled it, whether it will re-apply after a manual revert, and whether other services carry the same rewritten endpoint. No dispatch examined the automation source or any service beyond the eleven queried.

A ~5-minute gap sits between the config change (03:37:46), the alert (03:40:15) and the earliest crash-loop lines retained (03:42:57). tr_37309257e4ed notes normal cart traffic at 03:30 but log retention dropped the middle of the window, so the exact moment cartservice first failed to start is unestablished.

checkoutservice's error ratio peaks near 0.67, not 1.0 (tr_ca11e72b37a1), while every sampled trace carries ERROR (tr_34e02e3f107e). These are not obviously consistent. The residual successes may fall in the gaps between cart restarts, or the trace sample may be biased — unresolved, and tr_ca11e72b37a1 could not return per-timestamp values to locate the inflection.

Triage reported 12 services and 4 unmeasured edges crossed; only cart, checkout, payment, currency and productcatalog were examined. Whether the remaining services are merely starved of traffic (as in the cart-bad-image-tag corpus case) or independently impaired was never checked.

tr_38879161549e flags that an empty change log only equals 'nothing happened' if the pipeline captures all change types; out-of-band or manual changes on any service would be invisible to every changes dispatch here.
